new_groups.label: The kings, princes and states at war with France
new_groups.definition: Printings of a list from a London paper of early April 1793 of the powers combined against France, from the King of Great Britain and the Empress of Russia to the princes of the Empire. Three papers print it as 'An account of the Kings, Princes, and States engaged against the Republic of France', three as 'a list of the combination of Kings, Princes, and States, at war with France', a combination 'without example in the annals of mankind'; the list is counted as one item. A report.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round two, 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: The London Gazette from Tournai, 3 May: the French attacks repulsed
new_groups.definition: Printings of a bulletin from the London Gazette, dated Tournai, 3 May 1793: on the 1st the French attacked the advanced posts of the left wing and of the centre of the combined army and were repulsed, with the loss of men and cannon. The British government's own account. Four papers print it after another Tournai paragraph on the preparations against Condé.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round two, 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: Hamilton's circular to the collectors, with the President's rules on neutrality
new_groups.definition: Printings of the circular of the Secretary of the Treasury to the collectors of the customs (Philadelphia, 4 August 1793): as repeated contraventions of neutrality had taken place in American ports, the collectors were to watch for vessels arming or equipping for the powers at war, with the schedule of 'Rules adopted by the President' on arming, equipping and prizes. The circular and its rules are one publication. An official document.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round two, 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: The President of the National Convention's declaration of a plot
new_groups.definition: Printings of the 'Declaration made by the President of the National Convention to the French Nation' (Paris, May 1793): after a scandalous scene in the galleries, he declared his conviction of a conspiracy, revealed to him by good citizens, to destroy the Convention, and his resolve to wait the event at his post. One man's declaration of an alleged plot.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round two, 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: A letter from Cadiz, 24 June: 'a hot war with the Spaniards and French'
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from a gentleman at Cadiz to his brother in New York, dated 24 June 1793 (New York, 12 August): 'a hot war with the Spaniards and French', a battle near Malaga reported won by the French, and news of the fleets. One writer's account, partly hearsay ('We had accounts').
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round two, 6-paper threshold for 1793).

new_groups.label: The commissioners' letter on General Dampierre's death
new_groups.definition: Printings of a letter from the commissioners of the National Convention with the army of the North, Valenciennes, 9 May 1793, read in the Convention: General Dampierre, whose thigh was carried away by a ball the day before, died that morning, regretted by the whole army. The French government's commissioners' own account.

dispositions_summary.method: Round two of 1793. Round one (release v0.10.0) admitted the stories with an item in 7 or more papers and proposed a 6-paper threshold for this year, because 1793 has only 6 to 8 papers in print at a time; the owner agreed on 2026-11-10. The candidates in 6 papers that round one listed were read again with phrase searches over all 1,751 pages of 1793 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round2.json, phrase_hits_round2.json), every hit was read, papers in print without a hit were searched with loose keywords, and every admitted printing was checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round2.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: For 1793 only, a story needs one printed item found in 6 or more newspapers, counted item by item, with the two titles of a renamed paper counted once and both scanned copies of a Kentucky Gazette issue counted once. Items that need framing stay out, and items in 6 papers were chosen, as items in 7 or 8 papers are in other years, to cover the months and kinds of news: single paragraphs of news digests that add neither (the Rome paragraph of 29 September 1792, the Paris 'sullen tranquillity' paragraph) and a rumour in two wordings (Captain Hacket's report that Dumouriez had taken Amsterdam, 4 + 2 papers) were not admitted. Dumouriez's address, in 6 papers, was already a sub-story of round one.

counted_item_by_item.The list of the powers at war with Franc: Printed with two introductions to one list: 'An account of the Kings, Princes, and States engaged against the Republic of France' (GUS, NGz, PG) and 'a list of the combination of Kings, Princes, and States, at war with France' (NHG, AHL, MIR). The list is one item, so they are counted together: 6 papers (3 + 3), a judgement call.
counted_item_by_item.Hamilton's circular and the President's: The circular of 4 August and the schedule of rules sent with it are one publication, counted once: 6 papers (NGz, GUS, NHG, AHL, MIR, EAG). Not in PG, CI or KG.
counted_item_by_item.The Tournai bulletin: NGz and GUS print it as the London Gazette's 'TOURNAI (Tournay), May 3'; NHG, AHL, MIR and PG print the same sentences after a paragraph on the preparations against Condé. PG printed it twice (22 July and 5 August).
counted_item_by_item.Dampierre's death: The commissioners' letter of 9 May follows their letter of 8 May on the attack (4 papers), which is not part of the group. The Kentucky Gazette's two scanned copies of 14 September count once.

not_admitted.Left out for framing (6 papers): The War Office paragraph on the treaty commissioners at the Rapids of the Miami, the German Creek letter on a raid on the 'valley Indian towns', Captain Fanning's account of the burning of Cap Francais and the brig Mary's report of the dead there; they need framing first (outputs/story_discovery_1793/README.md).
not_admitted.Not recommended at 6 papers: The Rome paragraph of 29 September 1792 and the Paris 'sullen tranquillity' paragraph (single digest paragraphs, in months already covered) and Captain Hacket's Amsterdam rumour (two wordings, 4 + 2).
